animals.name: Neocaridina shrimp (red)
animals.notes: The four colour groups share one tank and interbreed freely, so the lines will trend toward wild brown over successive generations. Separating a line needs a second tank, not a divider.

animals.name: Neocaridina shrimp (yellow)
animals.notes: Interbreeds with the other colour groups in this tank.

animals.name: Neocaridina shrimp (red and white)
animals.notes: Interbreeds with the other colour groups in this tank.

animals.name: Neocaridina shrimp (orange and white)
animals.notes: Interbreeds with the other colour groups in this tank.

animals.name: Fancy guppy
animals.notes: Sex ratio unknown. If mixed, fry within weeks and a compounding bioload. Guppies take shrimplets, so recruitment in a shared tank depends on cover.

animals.name: Albino mystery snail
animals.notes: Adults are commonly given 2.5-5 gal each, so this group is the largest single bioload in the tank. Shell condition is the health signal to watch.

animals.name: Red Racer nerite
animals.notes: Grazes biofilm only and cannot breed in fresh water, so this group only ever shrinks. Losses are not replaced from within.

animals.name: Otocinclus
animals.notes: Species confirmed. Alone, and Otocinclus are shoaling animals - see the shoal minimum in `aqua species otocinclus`. The belly check is the health signal: rounded means feeding, flat or sunken is the warning.
